key_findings: **FUN_007663D0 is the +0x16C per-record bind state machine**, driven per-frame by FUN_00766F00 (BCS-Y-0135) via LuaFrameTick (BCS-Y-1701). Advances a control-record 0->10: register Debug/WorldMaster/CommandDebugger classes (0-5), load '/Area/' resource (7->8), record id == 0xC0000024 (8->9), +0x170 handle == 0xC0000024 (9->10 terminal).

**State 10 is the precondition for Lua-binding**: only at +0x16C==10 does FUN_00766F00 set actor+0x5C=1 + install the LuaActorImpl (client-architecture 'Zone-in actor bind and Lua-class-readiness pipeline'). So the dismiss chain (spawn -> bind-to-10 -> +0x5C -> _onPostWarp -> _fadeOut) hinges on the MyPlayer-control record reaching state 10.

**Two concrete checkable blocker gates**: (1) the '/Area/' resource must load (case 7, keyed off record+0x2b); (2) the record id AND its +0x170 paired handle must both reconcile to the MyPlayer-control SID 0xC0000024 (cases 8,9). The latter ties to the original handoff's actor-ID concern - if the spawn-burst's MyPlayer is not reconcilable to SID 0xC0000024 client-side, the bind stalls and the overlay never dismisses.

**0xC0000024 is a client-internal control-class SID** (the 0xc0000000-class, per the handle-class check in Application_FrameTick BCS-Y-1711). The server's MyPlayer spawn must drive the client to create/assign the local control at that SID - the next client-side layer to map.
